**Confirming Deletion**

I'm currently processing the implications of the `pyenv virtualenv-delete` command. My focus is on confirming whether this action extends to eradicating all installed packages within the specified virtual environment.

**Verifying Package Erasure**

I'm confirming that deleting a `pyenv` virtual environment inherently removes all associated installed packages, as they reside solely within the environment's directory structure which is then purged.

**Confirming Package Erasure**

I'm confirming that deleting a `pyenv` virtual environment inherently removes all associated installed packages, as they reside solely within the environment's directory structure which is then purged.
[/Thinking]

**Yes**, the packages installed in that specific virtual environment will be completely deleted. 

When you run `pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>`, pyenv completely removes the underlying directory that belongs to that virtual environment (usually located at `~/.pyenv/versions/<venv-name>`). 

Since all the packages you installed were saved inside that specific directory, they are permanently removed along with the environment.

**Note:** This will **not** affect packages installed in your global Python installation or any other pyenv virtual environments. Only the packages strictly isolated to `<venv-name>` will be deleted.
